chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Soloing when Redman and Benny Carter came late
summary: Smith played solos until the leaders arrived, told by Redman to stay on clarinet; he was with Redman about six months and Carter two months.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: And when you were on a gig with Don, did you never take any solos ever?

Mmm-hmm. Yeah. I took a solo when he wasn't there. See, he'd come to work late. He'd make us start, and he wouldn't start with us, and he'd come maybe an hour so later, and them boys would say, "Buster, you play Don's part. You take them solos and things in there." So I'd take the solos. And when he'd come, he'd say, "Get back on your clarinet. Don't play no alto, or you take the spotlight off me."
He knew you were better than he was.
You are better than he was.
So I did it. And Benny Carter... I'd do the same thing with Benny Carter.

He'd come in late, too, sometimes -- 30 minutes late, something like that. But always the band would start up, some of the boys, the older men in the band... There was a trumpet player, he'd start the band off on time. And Benny would come in, then I'd play a ...[YAWNS]... and I'd take a solo, and then Benny would get there and he'd take over and gave his solos. In other words, they had to fix it where they had the best numbers where he played his best solo... They wouldn't play them until he got there. That's the way they did that.
How long were you with Redman?
I was with Redman around about... It was about six months. And I was with Benny about a couple of months.
